Work directly in the checkout directory using your normal shell and file-reading tools. Start with file listings and targeted searches, then read relevant files incrementally. Respect the exclusions and keep the checkout unchanged. Do not dump the entire repository or read bundled source archives. Tool calls and results are retained in the session transcript.

Inspect the supplied codebase and identify its core component: the connected set of responsibilities around which the application's main behavior and state are organized. Generate a single ASCII tree diagram showing that core component's modular structure: its logical modules, what each exposes and keeps internal, and how they depend on one another. Choose the scope and level of detail that best explain the codebase. Ground the diagram in the source code.

Structure the tree as a modular decomposition of the core component:
  - Top-level branches are the core's main modules: logical-semantic groupings of responsibility, not directories or files. Each module appears in exactly one place.
  - Depth always means "belongs to": a child is a submodule, type or function grouped within its parent's responsibility.
  - Abstract away file-level organization, but keep boundaries: under each module, distinguish what it exposes to other modules from what it keeps internal.
  - Place dependency lines under the module that depends, with -> lines to the modules it uses. Other relationships appear only where they explain a boundary; do not organize the tree around them.
Cover breadth before depth:
  - Name every major module of the core, even in one line, before detailing any of them.
  - When a module has substantial internal structure, give it a child line naming its submodules, even if you do not expand them.
  - Do not detail one module down to individual helpers or fields while another major module remains a single line.

Here is the "3+1" model of conceptual codebase models:
1. [REPLACED] Containment	      where code lives
2. [REPLACED] Lexical scope	    which names code can see
  -> *collapse* into 1. Modular structure
    I want to collapse Containment / Lexical scope into a single category, called modular structure, which:
    - abstracts out the source file level organization
      - but retains boundaries and visibility: what a component exposes versus keeps internal
    - retains dependency graph
    - groups components into higher level, logic-semantical categorizations
3. Call (dynamic)     which activation invoked which
4. Ownership          responsibility for state, storage, resources, and their lifetimes: who creates, retains, changes, or releases them
1. [SPECIAL] Data dependency   is a different kind of thing. It isn’t a fifth organizational choice; it is the record of what actually needs what for the program to compute its result. It’s a graph, and it exists before you decide how to organize anything.

Keep the following in mind when generating your diagram:
  - there should be 60/40 between code refs and nat lang

Few-shot examples (synthetic style references, not source facts):
Example 1: Incremental compiler
Incremental compiler -- reuse follows the module dependency graph
|
|-- [M] BuildGraph connects source modules to their compilation artifacts
|   |-- modules[moduleId]: ModuleUnit
|   |   |-- sourceHash -> immutable source bytes
|   |   |-- imports[] -> resolved module identities
|   |   `-- interfaceHash -> names and types visible to consumers
|   `-- units[unitId]: AnalysisUnit
|       |-- mutually dependent modules share one unit
|       `-- dependencies[] -> units whose interfaces must be available first
|
|-- [C] compileUnit(unitId) resolves one reusable result
|   |-- [D] member source hashes + dependency interfaces + compiler options
|   |   `-- analysisKey, including the compiler implementation version
|   |-- ArtifactCache.lookup(analysisKey)
|   |   |-- Hit -> recover typed modules and diagnostics
|   |   `-- Miss -> analyze the unit
|   |       |-- [C] Parser.parse(source) -> syntax with source spans
|   |       |-- [C] Binder.bind(syntax, dependencyInterfaces)
|   |       |   `-- Scope
|   |       |       |-- declarations[name] -> local Symbol
|   |       |       |-- parent -> enclosing lexical scope
|   |       |       `-- exports -> symbols visible across the module boundary
|   |       `-- [C] TypeChecker.check(boundUnit) -> typed modules + diagnostics
|   `-- Successful analysis -> Emitter.emit(typedModules, target)
|       |-- [D] typed modules + target version + emission options -> objectKey
|       `-- ObjectArtifact
|           |-- object code / exported interface / source map
|           `-- [O] ArtifactCache retains complete immutable entries
|               `-- consumers borrow artifacts; eviction follows cache policy
|
|-- [C] rebuild(changedPaths) propagates only relevant changes
|   |-- Capture new source hashes and resolve changed imports
|   |   `-- [D] updated graph -> regroup cycles and order affected units
|   |-- Reanalyze affected units
|   |   |-- Exported interface changed -> invalidate dependent analysis keys
|   |   `-- Interface unchanged -> consumers can reuse their typed modules
|   `-- [D] reachable object hashes + runtime + linker options -> bundleKey
|       `-- Linker.link(objects) produces the executable bundle
|           `-- changed implementation can require linking without retyping consumers
|
`-- [O] BuildScheduler controls transient execution
    |-- ready queue -> units whose dependency results are available
    |   `-- independent units may run concurrently
    |-- running[unitId] -> task + worker lease
    |   |-- [C] invoke compileUnit(unitId)
    |   `-- task settlement returns the worker lease
    |-- cancel(buildId)
    |   `-- stop scheduling -> signal tasks -> await settlement -> release snapshot
    `-- BuildResult retains bundle references and source-located diagnostics
        `-- [D] diagnostic spans + captured sources -> stable reported locations

Example 2: Telemetry ingestion service
Telemetry ingestion service
|
|-- [M] IngestGateway accepts batches from device connections
|   |-- accept(connection, envelope): BatchReceipt
|   |   |-- [D] credentials + device registry -> authorized tenant/device
|   |   `-- [C] decode -> validate envelope -> PartitionRouter.route(batch)
|   |       |-- Partition key = tenantId + deviceId
|   |       `-- One device's batches reach the same ordered partition
|   |-- [O] Retains connection state until disconnect
|   |   |-- pending[batchId] -> receipt waiter
|   |   `-- socket close detaches waiters; accepted work can still finish
|   `-- Admission limit
|       |-- available capacity -> enqueue batch
|       `-- full partition queue -> return retryable rejection
|
|-- [O] PartitionWorker owns one partition's ingestion progress
|   |-- Retained state
|   |   |-- queue: BoundedQueue<AcceptedBatch>
|   |   |   `-- accepted batches wait here before processing
|   |   |-- checkpoint: PartitionCheckpoint
|   |   |   |-- partitionId / committedOffset
|   |   |   `-- lastSequence[deviceId] -> latest committed device sequence
|   |   `-- lease: PartitionLease
|   |       |-- ownerId / epoch / expiresAt
|   |       `-- [D] current epoch -> authority to commit new progress
|   |
|   |-- [C] run() drains the queue one batch at a time
|   |   `-- process(batch)
|   |       |-- Establish batch identity
|   |       |   |-- key = tenantId + deviceId + batchId
|   |       |   `-- [C] EventStore.lookupReceipt(key)
|   |       |       |-- Same payload hash -> return committed receipt
|   |       |       |-- Different payload hash -> reject identity conflict
|   |       |       `-- Missing receipt -> prepare a new commit
|   |       |
|   |       |-- Normalize measurements
|   |       |   `-- [C] SchemaRegistry.resolve(batch.schemaVersion)
|   |       |       |-- [M] Exposes versioned field and unit definitions
|   |       |       `-- [D] raw samples + exact schema -> Measurement[]
|   |       |           |-- identity: tenantId / deviceId / sequence
|   |       |           |-- observation: timestamp / metric / value / unit
|   |       |           `-- provenance: batchId / schemaVersion / payloadHash
|   |       |
|   |       |-- Check sequence continuity
|   |       |   |-- [D] firstSequence + checkpoint.lastSequence[deviceId]
|   |       |   |   `-- next expected sequence or a detected gap
|   |       |   |-- Contiguous -> stage measurements
|   |       |   `-- Gap or overlap -> reject without advancing checkpoint
|   |       |
|   |       `-- Commit and acknowledge
|   |           |-- [C] EventStore.commit(batch, checkpoint, lease.epoch)
|   |           |   |-- [D] measurements + batch identity + next checkpoint
|   |           |   |   `-- one durable transaction
|   |           |   `-- Stale lease epoch -> reject the former owner
|   |           `-- After confirmed commit
|   |               |-- Install returned checkpoint
|   |               `-- Resolve gateway waiters with BatchReceipt
|   |                   `-- receipt confirms storage, not downstream indexing
|   |
|   `-- Lease loss or shutdown
|       |-- [C] Stop admission and stop dequeuing new work
|       |-- In-flight commit may have an uncertain outcome
|       |   `-- retry resolves through its durable batch receipt
|       `-- [O] Release queue entries and detach remaining waiters
|           `-- next owner restores progress from EventStore
|
|-- [M] EventStore binds stored events to durable progress
|   |-- [M] Exposes commit / lookupReceipt / restoreCheckpoint / scan
|   |-- Internal transaction
|   |   |-- Verify current partition lease epoch
|   |   |-- Append measurements with partition offsets
|   |   |-- Insert receipt under the unique batch identity
|   |   `-- Advance PartitionCheckpoint in the same commit
|   |       `-- failure rolls back events, receipt and checkpoint together
|   |-- [O] Retains the durable event log and retry receipts
|   |   |-- worker restarts leave both intact
|   |   `-- receipt retention defines the supported retry horizon
|   `-- scan(partitionId, afterOffset): EventPage
|       `-- [D] committed log + cursor -> ordered events and next cursor
|
`-- [M] ProjectionHost maintains independently rebuildable read models
    |-- [O] consumers[name]: ProjectionConsumer
    |   |-- cursor[partitionId] -> last applied event offset
    |   |-- handler: ProjectionHandler
    |   `-- cancellation + poll subscription
    |
    |-- Registered consumers
    |   |-- LatestReading
    |   |   |-- [D] device/metric + sequence -> newest accepted value
    |   |   `-- older replayed events cannot replace a newer reading
    |   `-- HourlySummary
    |       |-- [D] metric + observation timestamp -> aggregation bucket
    |       `-- count / sum / minimum / maximum
    |           `-- late observations update their original time bucket
    |
    |-- [C] poll() -> EventStore.scan() -> handler.apply(page)
    |   `-- Projection transaction
    |       |-- Apply only offsets beyond the stored consumer cursor
    |       `-- Save changed rows and cursor atomically
    |           `-- crash before commit -> safely read the same page again
    |
    `-- rebuild(name, newVersion)
        |-- [O] Create separate projection tables and fresh cursors
        |-- [C] Replay retained events while the current version serves reads
        `-- [D] rebuilt cursors + captured log positions -> readiness
            `-- switch readers after catch-up; retire the previous tables

Use the examples as a varied pool of representational choices. Let the supplied evidence determine depth, branching, density, and relationship types; do not copy their domain facts, exact shapes, counts, or require every tag.

Tree validation: Start with one root title, followed by a connector-only line. Place all other content beneath explicit branches. Do not insert annotations, references, legends, or explanatory text between the root title and its first branch.

Root title
|
|-- First component
|   `-- Supporting detail
`-- Second component

Before returning, verify that every branch belongs to the single root.

Return a JSON object with exactly one field, "ascii", containing the diagram string. Return exactly one ASCII tree with one root, printable ASCII characters, spaces and LF newlines. No Markdown fences or surrounding prose. The complete tree must fit within 20000 characters. Do not add separate side diagrams.

{"ascii":"Ghostty terminal-surface core -- interactive sessions centered on Surface and Termio.terminal
|
|-- [Host] Application and native-runtime boundary
|   |-- Exposes: App.create/destroy, tick, addSurface/deleteSurface, updateConfig
|   |   `-- apprt.App/Surface, Action, Target: native events in; UI requests out
|   |-- Internal: surface registry, focused_surface, app mailbox, shared resource lifetimes
|   |   |-- Runtime adapters: GTK, embedded, browser, none; selected at compile time
|   |   `-- App retains font_grid_set and renderer.Device; releases them after surfaces
|   |-- Boundary: native runtime decides windows/tabs/splits; core Surface is only a terminal widget
|   |-- -> [Session]: registers surfaces and dispatches their messages
|   |-- -> [Config], [Font], [Render]: configuration and application-wide resources
|   `-- Sources: src/App.zig:22-198; src/apprt.zig:1-58; src/Surface.zig:1-11
|
|-- [Session] Surface lifecycle and shared-state coordination
|   |-- Exposes: Surface.init/deinit/close, handleMessage, updateConfig, draw
|   |   `-- sizeCallback, focusCallback, occlusionCallback: geometry and visibility updates
|   |-- Shared contract: renderer.State contains a Terminal pointer, mutex, preedit and mouse data
|   |   `-- lockDemand/unlockDemand/yieldToDemand prevent hot IO from starving frame snapshots
|   |-- Internal: per-surface worker assembly, DerivedConfig, size, focus, child-exit policy
|   |   |-- Subparts: renderer worker, IO worker, optional search worker and inspector attachment
|   |   `-- deinit stops/joins workers before destroying shared state and dereferencing fonts
|   |-- -> [Host]: rt_app.performAction and rt_surface.close delegate native UI work
|   |-- -> [IO], [Render], [Font]: constructs session resources and connects their handles
|   |-- -> [Config], [Search], [Inspect]: applies settings and manages optional facilities
|   `-- Sources: src/Surface.zig:69-188,477-895,1017,1804,2600,3437-3466;
|       src/renderer/State.zig:13-111
|
|-- [Input] User interaction, local actions and terminal input encoding
|   |-- Exposes: Surface.keyCallback/textCallback/preeditCallback, mouseButtonCallback,
|   |   |-- scrollCallback, performBindingAction, completeClipboardRequest
|   |   `-- input.KeyEvent, Binding.Action, InputEffect; key_encode.encode, mouse_encode.encode
|   |-- Internal: binding precedence, key-table stack, queued key sequences, mouse capture
|   |   |-- Subparts: key remapping/bindings, keyboard protocols, mouse reporting,
|   |   |   selection gestures, links, clipboard/paste and IME handling
|   |   `-- Binding handling precedes byte encoding; terminal modes determine encoding options
|   |-- -> [Config]: keybindings, remaps and interaction policy
|   |-- -> [VT]: mode-sensitive encoders, selection and viewport state
|   |-- -> [Session], [IO]: shared-state locking and queued terminal input
|   |-- -> [Host], [Render], [Inspect]: UI actions, visual feedback and optional event recording
|   `-- Sources: src/Surface.zig:2669-2987,3326-3426,3584,3918,4941,6017;
|       src/input.zig:10-37; src/input/key_encode.zig:14-82; src/input/mouse_encode.zig:13-81
|
|-- [Config] Configuration resolution and reloadable policy
|   |-- Exposes: Config.default/load/loadFile/loadIter/finalize, clone, changeConditionalState
|   |-- Internal: arena-backed values, diagnostics and replay steps
|   |   |-- Subparts: default files, CLI arguments, recursive files, themes and conditionals
|   |   `-- load resolves defaults, default files, CLI and recursive files before finalize
|   |-- Boundary: consumers derive their own configuration instead of retaining caller Config pointers
|   |-- -> [Input]: Keybinds and default bindings; -> [Render]: padding/geometry configuration types
|   `-- Sources: src/config/Config.zig:42,4035-4110,4428,4552,4751,5205,6647;
|       src/App.zig:168-198; src/Surface.zig:144-147; src/termio/Termio.zig:182-245
|
|-- [IO] Process transport and application-facing terminal protocol effects
|   |-- Exposes: Termio.init/deinit, processOutput, queueMessage, resize, focusGained
|   |   `-- termio.Message/Mailbox and Backend.queueWrite provide asynchronous work boundaries
|   |-- Internal: Termio owns Terminal, terminal_stream, backend and derived settings
|   |   |-- Exec/Subprocess: PTY, command/environment, shell integration and process-exit handling
|   |   |-- Exec.ReadThread: output ingestion; termio.Thread: writer loop and control messages
|   |   |-- StreamHandler.vt/vtPrintAscii: applies terminal actions and handles external effects
|   |   `-- Timers: resize coalescing, selection scrolling and synchronized-output reset
|   |-- Boundary: processOutput locks shared state; ordinary parsing uses terminal_stream.nextSlice
|   |-- -> [VT]: parses escape sequences and mutates the renderer-independent terminal model
|   |-- -> [Session]: shared lock and surface mailbox for title, clipboard and child-exit requests
|   |-- -> [Render]: wakeups/messages request repaint; -> [Config]: process and terminal policy
|   |-- -> [Inspect]: optional PTY recording switches parsing to byte-at-a-time inspection
|   `-- Sources: src/termio/Termio.zig:1-76,254,437,524,705-763;
|       src/termio/Thread.zig:1-98; src/termio/Exec.zig:86,274,403,624,1305;
|       src/termio/backend.zig:13-86; src/termio/stream_handler.zig:188-254
|
|-- [VT] Terminal protocol interpretation and authoritative screen state
|   |-- Exposes: Terminal operations, Stream(Handler), Stream.Action and RenderState
|   |   |-- Terminal: print, cursor movement, mode changes, resize and scrollViewport
|   |   `-- Stream: next/nextSlice dispatch typed actions; RenderState: beginUpdate/endUpdate
|   |-- Internal: protocol decoding and terminal storage, independent of the GPU/native UI
|   |   |-- Parsing: Parser, UTF8Decoder, CSI/OSC/DCS/APC handling and continuation tracking
|   |   |-- ScreenSet: primary/alternate Screen, cursor, tracked selection and keyboard flags
|   |   |-- PageList/Page: cells, rows, styles, graphemes, scrollback, reflow and compression
|   |   |-- Protocol state: modes, colors, tabstops, hyperlinks, semantic prompts and Kitty images
|   |   `-- Render extraction: dirty rows/cells, highlights and image placements
|   |-- Boundary: generic Stream invokes its supplied handler; PTY writes and native UI effects
|   |   remain the handler's responsibility, not requirements of the terminal model
|   `-- Sources: src/terminal/Terminal.zig:1-175; src/terminal/stream.zig:588-673;
|       src/terminal/ScreenSet.zig:18-106; src/terminal/Screen.zig:40-98;
|       src/terminal/PageList.zig:1278,3347,5431,6313; src/terminal/render.zig:289,941,1423
|
|-- [Render] Frame construction, scheduling and GPU presentation
|   |-- Exposes: Renderer(GraphicsAPI), Device, Thread.Mailbox, renderer.Message and Health
|   |   `-- updateFrame, drawFrame, setFontGrid, setScreenSize, changeConfig
|   |-- Internal: renderer.Thread event loop, wakeups, cursor blink and animation scheduling
|   |   |-- Frame preparation: terminal snapshot, text shaping, cells, images and overlays
|   |   |-- Frame resources: SwapChain, FrameState, textures/buffers and custom shaders
|   |   `-- GraphicsAPI: compile-time Metal or OpenGL implementation
|   |-- Boundary: updateFrame captures Terminal under lock; RenderState finishes processing
|   |   outside the critical section; synchronized_output can suspend frame updates
|   |-- -> [Session]: shared renderer.State and presentation notifications
|   |-- -> [VT]: dirty-state extraction, image placements and viewport information
|   |-- -> [Font]: shaping, glyph lookup and atlas textures
|   |-- -> [Host], [Config]: native presentation surface and rendering settings
|   `-- Sources: src/renderer.zig:15-44; src/renderer/Thread.zig:25-82;
|       src/renderer/generic.zig:321-556,1317,1371-1515,1716,2171,2249
|
|-- [Font] Font resolution, shaping and reusable glyph resources
|   |-- Exposes: SharedGridSet.ref/deref, SharedGrid.getIndex/renderGlyph/cellSize,
|   |   `-- Metrics, Shaper, ShaperCache and Atlas
|   |-- Internal: configuration-keyed grids and their reference counts
|   |   |-- Discovery/fallback: Discover, Collection, DeferredFace and CodepointResolver
|   |   |-- Shaping backends: HarfBuzz, CoreText, noop or web_canvas, selected by font backend
|   |   `-- Raster resources: grayscale/color atlases, codepoint/glyph caches and SharedGrid.lock
|   |-- Boundary: compatible surfaces share a grid; font changes acquire a replacement grid
|   |   rather than mutating every surface's font configuration through the shared instance
|   |-- -> [Config]: font descriptors/features; -> [VT]: terminal-row shaping inputs
|   |-- -> [Render]: CellSize geometry contract
|   `-- Sources: src/font/main.zig:7-31; src/font/SharedGrid.zig:1-64,143,156,379;
|       src/font/SharedGridSet.zig:96,413,476,560; src/font/shape.zig:1-65
|
|-- [Search] Incremental search over terminal content
|   |-- Exposes: search.Thread.init/threadMain/deinit, Mailbox and EventCallback
|   |   |-- Message.change_needle/select requests
|   |   `-- Event.complete/total_matches/selected_match/viewport_matches results
|   |-- Internal: TerminalSearch, ScreenSearch, refresh timer and notification-difference state
|   |   `-- Subparts: active-area, viewport, page-list and sliding-window search
|   |-- Boundary: copies terminal data to reduce lock time; viewport_matches memory is valid
|   |   only during its callback; Surface owns the optional worker's lifetime
|   |-- -> [VT]: screens, tracked highlights and terminal data
|   |-- -> [Session]: supplied terminal/mutex and result callback; Session forwards UI/render updates
|   `-- Sources: src/terminal/search/Thread.zig:1-24,47-139,506-588;
|       src/Surface.zig:210-227,1485-1608
|
`-- [Inspect] Optional terminal diagnostics
    |-- Exposes: Inspector.setup/init/deinit, recordKeyEvent, recordPtyRead, render, rendererInfo
    |-- Internal: ImGui widget state and bounded keyboard-event history
    |   `-- Subparts: surface/mouse inspection, key stream, VT stream and renderer information
    |-- Boundary: activation is per Surface; ordinary sessions need not record diagnostic streams
    |-- -> [Session], [VT]: inspected surface and terminal state
    |-- -> [Font]: embedded inspector font
    `-- Sources: src/inspector/Inspector.zig:1-120; src/Surface.zig:934-993;
        src/termio/Termio.zig:737-758"}
